title: Chapter 24 — Smart Home & Connected Appliances
intro: What smart features actually do, honest use-case selling, privacy, and integration.

sections.title: The Honest Smart Appliance Conversation
sections.content:
Smart appliance features range from genuinely useful to marketing fluff. Your job is to know the difference and be honest about it.

Genuinely useful: remote diagnostics that tell the service tech what is wrong before they arrive. Cycle notifications so you know when laundry is done. Energy monitoring. Automatic reordering of detergent pods or water filters.

Situationally useful: interior cameras on refrigerators — great for checking what you need while grocery shopping. Smart recipe integration on ovens — useful for serious home cooks, irrelevant for everyone else. Voice control — convenient for some, gimmicky for others.

Rarely used: most built-in touchscreens. Complex app-only features that require multiple steps. Smart features that require a separate hub or subscription.

sections.title: Platform Ecosystem
sections.content:
The major smart platforms in appliances are Home Connect (BSH — Bosch, Thermador, Gaggenau), SmartThings (Samsung), ThinQ (LG), and SmartHQ (GE Appliances, Café, Monogram).

When a customer is buying multiple appliances, platform consistency matters. A kitchen with all Bosch appliances talks to one Home Connect app. Mix Samsung and LG and the customer needs two apps. This is a legitimate selling point for brand consistency.

WiFi connectivity requires a stable home network. If the customer's WiFi is weak in the kitchen, smart features will frustrate them. Ask about their home network setup before selling hard on smart features.

sections.title: Privacy and the Honest Disclosure
sections.content:
Some customers ask about data collection. Be straightforward. Smart appliances do collect usage data — when you run cycles, what settings you use, energy consumption. Most manufacturers use this for product improvement and diagnostics.

The customer who is privacy-conscious should know: you can usually use the appliance fully without connecting it to WiFi. The smart features are optional. The appliance works perfectly without them.

Never oversell smart features to a customer who does not care about them. If they want a reliable dishwasher that cleans well and runs quietly, the smart features are a footnote, not a headline. Sell the product first. Mention the smart features as a bonus, not a justification for the price.
